rationale: Verified against the current checkout. The desktop platform is Electron (apps/stage-tamagotchi); the legacy Tauri `crates/` directory is gone (Tauri appears only in historical blog posts), and the answer correctly treats Electron as current rather than any legacy platform. Nearly every cited path, line range, and symbol checks out: ExtensionHost lifecycle (announced/active/degraded/withdrawn bindings), manifest v1 contract (shared/types.ts:233-253), three built-in kits (widget/gamelet/tool), extensions-v1.json persistence + static-assets + auto-reload (plugins/host), ServerManager ordered start/reverse stop, channel-server WebSocket/TLS/QR pairing, the 14-window manager inventory with reusable/referenced primitives, plugin-sdk private:true + exports, permission default (resolvedGrant falls back to manifest.permissions when permissionResolver is absent), incompatible-version declared but unchecked in resolveKitApi, websocket/web-worker/node-worker transport stubs, ExposePolicy declared but unenforced, plugin-protocol delivery/RouteTargetExpression defined but unused by the desktop app, sandbox:false across windows, and the three-way exit lifecycle. The answer scores full marks on all nine dimensions: it classifies scope with confidence, grounds claims in evidence, explains where friction spreads and why, gives explicit quality-attribute trade-offs, compares three viable options including the status quo, makes a recommendation that follows from the stated drivers, and lays out a six-step incremental, observable, reversible migration with concrete verification (grep exit criteria, regression/golden tests, typecheck/lint/vitest). The four recorded errors are minor counting or citation nits and do not contradict the architecture findings or the recommendation. Total 18/18.
